rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a 3BB blastocyst and appropriately describes expanded blastocyst, loose ICM and TE, but relies heavily on the provided Gardner grade and adds confidence about distinct structures and lack of degeneration that may not be clearly verifiable from the image alone.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve markers, sperm parameters, endometrium, lifestyle, and first-cycle status well with embryo quality, though it overemphasizes contradiction in the DOR diagnosis without full context.

Reasoning is mostly logical and structured, but there are some overstatements and mild inconsistencies, especially the very optimistic implantation estimate and the strong claim that ovarian reserve is excellent despite the stated diagnosis.

SET recommendation and general counseling are guideline-concordant, but suggesting ERA after one failed transfer and implying freeze-all/FET may improve outcomes in this good-prognosis first cycle are not strongly guideline-based; PGT-A is also presented somewhat too readily for a 29-year-old.

Provides clear practical next steps for current transfer and contingency planning, including SET, luteal support, and follow-up options, though some recommendations are broader than necessary for this specific first-cycle case.
